title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (§10 of the notes, 'déploiement'). A stratified space X has strata indexed by a poset I. The unfolding replaces each stratum by a compact manifold with boundary (more generally with corners) Σ_i. For every flag (strict chain) d=(i_1<...<i_n) in I there is a space Σ_d. Two kinds of maps relate them. If d is an initial segment of d', there is a fibration Σ_{d'}→Σ_d. If d is a final ('cofinal') segment of d', there is an embedding Σ_{d'}↪Σ_d into the boundary. Σ_{ij} is the 'link bundle': it fibres over Σ_i and sits in the boundary of Σ_j. The previous page has established, under the quasi-singularity condition (e) and the non-singularity condition (f), that the fibres of Σ_{ij}→Σ_i are manifolds with boundary.

Struck-out top paragraph (the case d=(i), d'=(i,j)). The boundary of the fibre of Σ_{ij}→Σ_i is stratified by the Σ_{d''}, where d'' runs over flags strictly containing (i,j), with first element i and last element j. Equivalently d'' runs over the nonempty chains in the open interval I_{i<·<j}, i.e. Drap(I_{i<j}). Hence the excluded pair (∅,∅): without excluding it one would stratify Σ_{ij} itself rather than its boundary. This set is empty iff j covers i (j is an immediate successor of i). So Σ_{ij}→Σ_i is smooth, i.e. has closed-manifold fibres, iff i⋖j. A struck phrase 'j maximal in I' is a slip that he discarded.

General statement (kept). Let d=(i_1..i_p) be a proper initial segment of d'=(i_1..i_n), and write d'=d⊔d'_0 with d'_0=(i_{p+1}..i_n).
- The fibration Σ_{d'}→Σ_d has fibres that are manifolds with boundary (corners).
- The boundary of the fibre is stratified 'cylindrically' by the Σ_{d''} with d''⊋d'.
- d' must be cofinal in d'' (same top element i_n), so that Σ_{d''}↪Σ_{d'}.
- d must be an initial segment of d'', so that Σ_{d''}→Σ_d remains fibred.
- So d''=d⊔d''_0 with d''_0⊂I_{>i_p}, d''_0⊋d'_0, and d''_0 has the same maximum as d'_0.
- New elements can therefore only be inserted into the gaps (i_p,i_{p+1}),...,(i_{n-1},i_n).
- The boundary strata thus correspond bijectively to tuples of chains (e_1,...,e_{n-p}), e_k a possibly empty chain in I_{i_{p+k-1}<·<i_{p+k}}, not all empty. He writes this as Drap(I_{i_p<·<i_{p+1}} ⊔ ... ⊔ I_{i_{n-1}<·<i_n}).

Geometric meaning. The fibre of Σ_{d'}→Σ_d is (locally) a product of the successive link-fibres F_{i_p i_{p+1}} × ... × F_{i_{n-1}i_n}. This is a manifold with corners whose face poset is the product of the cones on the individual face posets, minus the all-interior face. The next page draws the consequence that the relevant chains are maximal-refinement chains in which each term covers the previous one. It then begins a digression replacing the discrete poset I by a topological poset with a semi-simplicial space of strict chains Σ*(n).

Purpose: the combinatorics of the boundary/corner structure of the iterated fibration ('resolution into manifolds with corners') of a Thom–Mather-type stratified space, indexed by the nerve of the stratification poset.
errors: The kept formula Drap(I_{i_p<·<i_{p+1}} ⊔ ... ⊔ I_{i_{n-1}<·<i_n}) is literally wrong if ⊔ means the coproduct of posets. Chains in a coproduct live in a single summand, but the boundary strata need tuples of chains, one per gap. The correct object is the ordinal sum/join I_{i_p<·<i_{p+1}} ⋆ ... ⋆ I_{i_{n-1}<·<i_n} (equivalently nonempty elements of ∏(Drap∪{∅})). The struck-out phrase 'privé de (∅,∅)' and the previous page's product formula Dép(..)×Dép(..) show he had the product-of-cones picture in mind; it is a notational slip, not a conceptual error.
Struck-out: the condition 'j maximal in I' for smoothness of Σ_{ij}→Σ_i is wrong; only 'j covers i' is needed. Grothendieck himself deleted it.
'Cofinal' is used in the sense 'has the same maximal element', which is implicit; with this reading the statements are correct.
The 'fibration' claims rely on the quasi-singularity (e) and non-singularity (f)/(g) hypotheses of the previous page and are not proved here.

ideas.what: Unfolding of a stratified space into manifolds with boundary/corners Σ_d indexed by flags of the stratum poset, with fibrations to initial segments and boundary embeddings from final segments.
ideas.modern_name: Resolution of a Thom–Mather stratified space into a manifold with corners with an iterated fibration structure; 'unzipping' of conically smooth stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather (control data, 1969–70), Verona (resolutions, 1970s–1984), Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza / Albin–Melrose (iterated fibration structures, ~2009–2012), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzipping, 2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (programmatic mention of 'déploiement' and 'théorie des voisinages tubulaires' for stratified spaces), without these details

ideas.what: The fibre of Σ_{ij}→Σ_i has empty boundary iff j covers i in I, i.e. the link-bundle is smooth exactly across codimension-one adjacencies of the poset.
ideas.modern_name: Boundary hypersurfaces/faces of the resolved link indexed by chains in the open interval (i,j)
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in Albin–Melrose and in the AFT unzip combinatorics

ideas.what: The boundary stratification of the fibre of Σ_{d'}→Σ_d is indexed by refinements of d' inside the gaps (i_p,i_{p+1}),...,(i_{n-1},i_n), i.e. the join of the open intervals (product of cones minus apex): a face poset of a product of manifolds with corners.
ideas.modern_name: Face poset of the iterated link; nerve of the join of open intervals of the stratification poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in the theory of manifolds with corners / iterated edge structures

missed.claim: An explicit flag-indexed description, ca. 1981–82, of the resolution of a stratified space into manifolds with corners. It gives the fibration/embedding functoriality along initial/final segments and the identification of the boundary of the link-fibres with chains in open intervals of the poset. This anticipates the later 'iterated fibration structure' formalism (Albin–Melrose et al.) and AFT unzipping. Grothendieck's archive version is not cited there; only the programmatic Esquisse mention is public.
missed.quote: la fibration Σ_{d'} → Σ_d est à fibres des variétés à bord, et les fibres des bords est stratifié [cylindriquement] par les Σ_{d''} ... corresp. biunivoque avec Drap(I_{i_p<·<i_{p+1}} ⊔ ... ⊔ I_{i_{n-1}<·<i_n})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical credit: it documents that Grothendieck had worked out the combinatorics of déploiement in detail, close to the modern resolution/unzipping theory. Mathematically it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, essentially correct combinatorial description of the corner structure of the unfolding of a stratified space. It matches what later appeared (Verona; Albin–Melrose iterated fibration structures; AFT unzipping), so it is not new mathematics today. It is a notable unpublished detail behind the Esquisse's 'déploiement' programme, but not a hidden result.
transcription_corrections: 'stratifié cycliquement[?]' should almost certainly read 'stratifié cylindriquement' (cf. 'stratification cylindrique' on the previous page).
'Σ_{(i,j)≠}' in the struck top paragraph is probably the fibre of Σ_{ij} (or Σ_{(i,j)} itself) 'lui-même, non de son bord'; the ≠ is likely a stray mark.
The 'Drap' in 'dans ≃ Drap(I_{i<j})' and in the final line is 'Drap' (flags), distinct from 'Dép' (déploiement) used on the previous page.
In the margin insertion 'et de la forme d ⊔ d''_0, où d''_0 ⊂ I_{>i_p}' the 'd' before 'drapeaux' should read 'd ⊔ d''_0 (drapeaux d''_0 ⊂ I_{>i_p})'.
'(hyp. C.T.)' in the left margin probably refers to a hypothesis label (e.g. 'conditions de transversalité/cylindricité'); reading uncertain.
